# Product backlog

This is the implementation tracking source of truth. The execution strategy and
definition of done live in [`README.md`](./README.md).

## Status and priority

- `done` — completed and validated; Evidence contains a commit.
- `in progress` — the single item currently being implemented.
- `next` — first item to pull after the current checkpoint.
- `ready` — sufficiently defined and waiting on its dependencies.
- `blocked` — cannot proceed until the named dependency or approval is resolved.
- `later` — intentionally ordered behind higher-priority work.
- `deferred` — outside the initial release.

Priorities describe product value, not strict technical order:

- `P0` — required for the mobile-first release.
- `P1` — backend/reliability work or mobile completeness needed before production.
- `P2` — admin-web delivery, the lowest-priority application surface.
- `P3` — explicitly deferred work.

With the process killed and the task still in Recents, Android brings the task to the front, recreates MainActivity with its old launcher intent, and hands the tap's FCM extras to `onNewIntent`, which Expo's `ReactActivityDelegateWrapper` drops while expo-updates delays the app's load (unchanged in expo 57.0.29). Fix: the config plugin `@pilates/mobile-core/launch-tap-plugin`, red `f3db1981` → `9f3924aa`, applied to both apps `4c2f4855`, forwards those extras to expo-notifications' `NotificationManager`, which keeps them until the JS emitter registers; a warm tap now reaches JS twice and opens once, because the message id was already deduplicated. Both apps need a new native build for the fix to reach devices. **Open:** the booking journey cannot run at night (no Session left today). Real iOS delivery waits for gate 9 (APNs key). Decisions taken under the blanket approval: React Native's own `Image` and a snapping `ScrollView` suffice (no expo-image, which is not in the app despite the brief, and no carousel library: no dependency commit); the list query keeps Home's `refetchOnMount: "always"` with the app defaults (staleTime 0, gcTime 5 min, refetch on foreground through the focus manager, no retry) and stays out of the ADR-0035 persisted allowlist, matching the API's `private, no-cache` (ADR-0063), while the immutable public images are left to the native image cache; a Promotion whose chosen image fails to load is dropped from the carousel (a card without its image is not a Promotion) and the list is re-read once per failed URL so a re-published image with new URLs comes back; the section hides completely when the list is empty or fails (Home never breaks for the carousel); pull to refresh refreshes every Home query, not only the carousel; the section label is the export's «Novedades del estudio»; the phone card is full width (UPL-002 sized the 960/1440 variants for a 345–400 css px card) and the tablet card stops at 720 pt with the next card peeking; the dots are the export's pill style; no tap target on a card. | MOB-051   | P2       | Client mobile       | Fix the conditional hook in Perfil: `profile-screen.tsx` calls `useClientPhoto` (which wraps TanStack `useQuery`) after its loading and failure returns, so the number of hooks changes when the profile query goes from loading to loaded or failed, which React reports as a change in the order of hooks and can throw «Rendered more hooks than during the previous render»; move the call above the early returns (the hook already accepts `null`) and cover the loading → loaded transition in `profile.spec.tsx`; then drop the `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` that MOB-050 left on the call | MOB-050 | Client 18 | done | Found by MOB-050's first lint run on 2026-10-07 (`react-hooks/rules-of-hooks`). The Simulator does not show it today because the persisted query cache usually restores the profile before Perfil mounts; a cold cache on a fresh install is the case to reproduce. **Compared with the code 2026-10-07** (twenty-seventh session, branch `fix/mob-051-perfil-conditional-hook`). The row was right about the defect and half right about why it stays hidden. `ProfileScreen` calls seven hooks before any return (`useNavigation`, `useMobileIdentity`, `useClientFetcher`, and the four generated query hooks for the profile, the subscription, the unread count, and the credit), then returns early while `profile.isPending` («Cargando…») and again when `profile.isError` or the response status is not 200 (`QueryFailure` with Reintentar), and only then calls `useClientPhoto`, which itself calls two hooks (`useClientFetcher`, that is `useContext`, and TanStack's `useQuery`, which adds several of its own: a context read, a `useState`, a `useSyncExternalStore`, effects). React 19.2.3 (the `react-native` 0.86.3 Fabric renderer, `ReactFabric-dev.js`) does not merely warn when the count grows between renders: during an update, the first hook call beyond the previous list makes `updateWorkInProgressHook` throw `Error("Rendered more hooks than during the previous render.")`, in development and in release builds alike; the development-only warning «React has detected a change in the order of Hooks called by ProfileScreen» is printed when a hook at a given position changes type, and the shrinking case throws «Rendered fewer hooks than expected». Nothing in the apps catches it (no error boundary in client-mobile or mobile-core), so the thrown error unmounts the root: a red box in Expo Go, a crash in a release build. The transition is reached twice: pending → loaded (a cold cache, Perfil mounted before the profile request answers) and failed → loaded (Reintentar after a failed profile request succeeds, which is the same screen instance going from `isError` to data). Why the Simulator never showed it: besides the persisted cache the row names, the Inicio tab mounts first and calls the same `useGetCurrentClientProfile`, so with the API on localhost the profile is settled milliseconds after login, long before a finger reaches the Perfil tab (React Navigation mounts the tab lazily on its first focus); the eight existing Perfil specs open Perfil through Inicio for the same reason and never render it pending, which is why they are green with the defect in place. The Design column said Client 10 (Pago); Perfil is screen 18, corrected here. No other screen calls a hook after an early return: lint's `rules-of-hooks` reports only this site, and a scan of the 113 hand-written `.tsx` files of client-mobile, staff-mobile, and mobile-core for a top-level hook call after a top-level `return` found the same single site (Staff Perfil's `account-avatar.tsx` and every other data screen call their hooks before branching). **Built 2026-10-07** (twenty-seventh session): red `16970245` (two specs in `profile-screen.spec.tsx`: one holds the `GET /clients/current` request behind a gate so Perfil mounts on «Cargando perfil» and then releases it, one answers 500 and then lets Reintentar succeed; both failed with «Rendered more hooks than during the previous render» thrown from `useClientPhoto`'s `useQuery`), green `aaa32d8e` (the `useClientPhoto` call moved up with the other seven hooks, fed `profile.data.data.photo?.imageAssetId ?? null` when the response is 200 and `null` otherwise, so its query stays disabled until the profile is loaded; the inline `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` and its comment went with the line they annotated; `use-client-photo.ts` untouched), `62d80617` (the gate's `release` typed `() => void`, found by typecheck), `e73efa8c` (at the user's request mid-session: `my-bookings.spec.tsx` and `reschedule-card.spec.tsx` keyed their stubbed `GET /sessions?…from…until` route by today's civil date while the screen asks for the Booking's own day, which is tomorrow's within an hour of midnight in Bolivia, so both failed at 23:13; they now derive the range from the Booking's `startsAt`), `8b5fd341` (the retry spec's 500 keeps failing until the spec releases it, because Inicio and Perfil both mount the profile query with `refetchOnMount: "always"` and a single failure was overtaken by the second mount's refetch once in the full run). What the sites do: (1) `BookingsScreen` seeds `noticeFor` from `route.params.confirmed.bookingId`, then the effect copies the same id again whenever `confirmed` changes and nulls it 8 s later; the strip renders while `noticeFor === confirmed.bookingId`, the param is never cleared; `session-detail-screen.tsx` (Reservar) and `reschedule-screen.tsx` (Reprogramar) navigate with `confirmed`; `session-detail.spec.tsx` «shows the Session facts and books…» and `my-bookings.spec.tsx` «reschedules a Booking…» assert «Reserva confirmada», `book-and-cancel-class.yaml` waits for it, nothing covers the fade. | MOB-053   | P3       | Mobile              | Catch render errors in both apps: neither client-mobile nor staff-mobile nor mobile-core has an error boundary, so a thrown render error (the kind MOB-051 fixed) unmounts the whole tree, a red box in Expo Go and a crash in a release build; wrap the navigators in a boundary that shows a recoverable «Algo salió mal» screen with a retry and reports the error, with a spec that throws from a child | MOB-051 | — | done | Opened by MOB-051 on 2026-10-07 while confirming that nothing catches «Rendered more hooks than during the previous render»; a design prompt may be needed for the recovery screen **Compared with the code 2026-10-08** (twenty-ninth session, branch `feature/mob-053-error-boundary`). The row was right: no error boundary exists in client-mobile, staff-mobile, or mobile-core (a grep for `componentDidCatch`, `getDerivedStateFromError`, `ErrorBoundary`, and `react-error-boundary` over the three packages finds nothing, and no package depends on `react-error-boundary`). Where the roots are composed: `MobileApplication` (`packages/mobile-core/src/application.tsx`) returns null until the fonts load and then nests `MobileQueryProvider` → `VerifiedLinkProvider` → `MobileIdentityProvider` → `IdentityNavigation`, which renders the app's `Navigation` once the identity is no longer restoring; `ClientNavigation` renders `AuthenticatedClientNavigation` (`createStaticNavigation` over the `ClientTabs` bottom-tab navigator and its four native stacks) inside a second `MobileQueryProvider` and the fetcher contexts when the role is `client`, otherwise `AuthenticationFlow` (or `EmailChangeLinkScreen` for a link); `StaffNavigation` picks one of the four `createStaticNavigation` Role stacks (`roleNavigation`) inside `MobileQueryProvider`, `StaffFetcherContext`, and `AssistantWorkspaceProvider`, otherwise `AuthenticationFlow`. What already renders a recoverable failure: `QueryFailure` (`ui/query-failure.tsx`: a centred `BodyText` with `accessibilityRole="alert"` and a `PrimaryButton` «Reintentar», no title) is what the data screens show with per-screen copy («No pudimos cargar tu inicio.», «No pudimos cargar la lista de asistencia.»); its action is the right one but it has no title or explanation, while `EmptyState variant="plain"` (`ui/empty-state.tsx`, MOB-040: a centred Lora 21 title, an optional 14 px muted note up to 260 px, an optional 220 px action, an optional quiet 34 px glyph) carries exactly the three pieces the row asks for, so the recovery screen reuses `Screen` + `EmptyState variant="plain"` + `PrimaryButton` and neither component changes (no glyph fits an error, so none is drawn). React Navigation: both apps are on `@react-navigation/native` 7.3.18 over core 7.21.13 with static navigators; the container lives inside each `createStaticNavigation` component and no state persistence is configured, so a boundary above it that remounts its subtree loses every tab and stack (the tree starts at the first route again); core 7 offers `screenLayout` on a navigator (and `layout` on a screen), a function that wraps each screen's element inside the navigator, which the React Navigation docs name as the place for an error boundary, so a boundary there replaces only the failed screen and keeps the navigator, its state, the tab bar, and the other tabs. How a thrown render error reaches the console today: React 19.2.3's Fabric renderer (`ReactFabric-dev.js`) routes it to the root's `onUncaughtError` when nothing catches it, the root unmounts, and RN's `setUpErrorHandling` hands it to `ExceptionsManager.handleException(e, true)`: the full-screen red box in Expo Go and a crash in a release build; with a boundary the renderer calls `onCaughtError`, which logs through `console.error` («An error occurred in the <X> component… React will try to recreate this component tree from scratch using the error boundary you provided»), and `ExceptionsManager.installConsoleErrorReporter` turns that into a red LogBox notification in development and a console line in release. «Reports the error» without a provider account therefore means `componentDidCatch` writing the error and the component stack through `console.error`; no Sentry, no new dependency. Design: no prompt draws a generic error state («Algo salió mal» and «inesperado» appear nowhere in `docs/design/prompts/` or `design/`; the 40 prompts that mention «error» are field errors, the Error tone, and the `QueryFailure` copies), and the README's «Cards» and «Lists between rules» sections describe only the framed and plain empty states, so follow-up 89 proposes the recovery screen (its states and copy) before it is built. **Built 2026-10-08** (twenty-ninth session). Follow-up 89 (`c620e66d`, `docs/design/prompts/followups/89-recovery-screen.md`, indexed 🕓 pending and listed under «Pending design exports») proposes the recovery screen as the plain empty state with an action: «Algo salió mal» (Lora 21), the note «No pudimos mostrar esta pantalla. Inténtalo de nuevo; si vuelve a pasar, cierra la app y ábrela otra vez.» (14 px muted, 260 px), and the regular «Reintentar» primary button, no card, no icon, one «Pantalla de recuperación» card in the design system and a README section; the apps are built from that copy and the export is design accuracy only. The row is half right. The warnings are real: a clean-shell `jest --ci` run of `main` prints 383 `console.error` blocks in client-mobile and 53 in staff-mobile, of three kinds: «An update to <X> inside a test was not wrapped in act(...)» (133 / 27; `HomeScreen` 35, `BrowseSessionsScreen` 26, `ProfileScreen` 16, `ProfileTabButton` 14, `BottomTabView` 10… in the Client app, `AccountAvatar` 8, `TrainerAgendaScreen` 6, `StaffProfileScreen` 6… in the Staff app), every one of them thrown from TanStack's `notifyManager` batch timer (`notifyManager.ts:42`, a `setTimeout` that delivers query results to their observers after a spec's last assertion); «The current testing environment is not configured to support act(...)» (247 / 26), thrown from React Navigation's `PreventRemoveProvider` effect and from the same TanStack timer while the act environment is off but an act scope is still open; and no «overlapping act» yet. The causes are in the specs, not in the app: RNTL 14 made `render`, `fireEvent`, `cleanup`, `rerender`, and `unmount` asynchronous (each is an `act(async …)` that flips `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` on and restores it when its promise settles), and 61 statement-level `fireEvent.*` calls in 14 spec files (`purchase-flow` 11, `profile-screen` 10, `client-shortcuts` 7, `staff-profile` 6, `session-detail` 6, `trainer-flows` 5…) plus one in `profile-test-support.tsx`'s `openProfile`, and 52 `cleanup()` calls in `afterEach` blocks of 50 files, are not awaited, so their act scope is still open when the next `waitFor` turns the environment off to poll: React then reports every update that lands in that window. RNTL 14 never sets `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` globally (its `act.js` sets it to true inside its own `act` and restores the previous value, `undefined`), so an update between two awaited calls is reported as «not configured» rather than flushed. The open handle is not real: on `main`, `jest --ci` without `--forceExit` exits on its own in mobile-core (4.5 s after start, 226 tests), client-mobile (7.0 s, 140), and staff-mobile (12.2 s, 116), and three scratch specs (empty, an import of `Text`, a rendered `Text`) exit at once; `--detectOpenHandles` on `app-shell.spec.tsx` ran for five minutes without naming a handle because there is none to name. The line «Force exiting Jest: Have you considered using `--detectOpenHandles`» that every run shows is printed by Jest whenever `--forceExit` is passed, whatever the handles; the 2026-09-22 note that staff-mobile «hangs after the summary» predates the NetInfo and AsyncStorage mocks in `jest.setup.ts` and no longer reproduces. The suspects the row names (TanStack's persister, the AppState and NetInfo subscriptions, the navigators) are all cleaned up by `MobileQueryProvider`'s effect or mocked in the setup. `--forceExit` therefore stays only where it is harmless (the CI workflow and the testing guide pass it; dropping it is a one-line chore outside this row's «spec files, `jest.setup.ts`, and test support» scope and is left as a leftover). The row is right. `AuthenticationFlow` seeds `route` from the intent it mounts with and, since MOB-052 (`9a5711d7`), adjusts it during render when the `intent` prop changes («state adjusted when a prop changes»); `usePendingRegistration` starts the once-per-launch restore at mount when the flow mounts without a link (`restore: intent === null || intent === undefined`), renders nothing while `restoring`, and when `store.load` settles with a kept registration sets it and calls the `onRestored` it captured at mount, which is `() => setRoute("check-email")` unconditionally. The Client app mounts the flow with no intent at a cold start and `VerifiedLinkProvider` delivers the startup link a moment later (`getInitialURL` is asynchronous), so the order «mount → restore starts → link arrives → route = verify-email → load settles → route = check-email» is the normal cold-start order on a device whose Client kept a registration and then tapped the email's link: the link's screen is overwritten by «Revisa tu correo», the token is never verified, and the Client is told to check the email she just came from. `VerifyEmailScreen` verifies on mount, so the overwrite also happens before the request is sent (the flow renders null while restoring). The two guard specs of MOB-052 («verifies the token once…», «restores once however often the flow re-renders meanwhile») hold `store.load` open and re-render the flow, but neither delivers an intent during the load. Rule to take: **the link's screen wins** (a link is a deliberate act by the person; a kept registration is a convenience that is still there afterwards), and **the kept registration stays stored and loaded**, so «Revisa tu correo» is reachable again on the next launch without a link, and the lapsed-registration cleanup still runs. The narrowest change is in the flow, not the hook: `onRestored` moves to «check-email» only while the route is still `login`, through a functional `setRoute`, so a route a link chose meanwhile is kept; the hook's once-per-launch effect, its effect event, and its `setPendingState(kept)` are untouched. **Built 2026-10-08** (twenty-ninth session). The row is redefined above: the flag goes once the Linux handle is found; that investigation is outside the one-line scope this row was opened with. **Decisions taken under the blanket approval**: (1) the workflow change is reverted on the branch rather than left red, so the pull request can be merged as a draft-turned-ready for the row and the Test 8 note alone, or closed; (2) the row stays `ready` with the real work named, not `blocked` (nothing external blocks it); (3) the admin-web step is untouched throughout. **Compared with the code 2026-10-08** (thirty-first session, branch `chore/mob-057-linux-jest-handle`, from `main` with pull requests 16 and 17 merged). The row is right that the linger lasts five to six minutes and shows only on CI, and wrong about where to look: none of its suspects holds a handle, and the difference is not the operating system but the worker count. What each setup does: all three mock `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` with its in-memory Jest mock and `@react-native-community/netinfo` with an `addEventListener` that returns a no-op unsubscribe, so neither owns a timer or a socket; the two app setups also deliver TanStack's `notifyManager` notifications synchronously (no batch timer since MOB-054) and mock expo-crypto, the Client one expo-image-picker, expo-image-manipulator, and expo-file-system too; `react-native-screens` and the `AppState` listener are mocked by jest-expo's and React Native's presets (`AppState.addEventListener` returns a subscription whose `remove` the `MobileQueryProvider` effect calls on unmount), and the persister's only timer is `asyncThrottle`'s one-second `setTimeout`. The handle is TanStack Query's garbage collection: `Removable.scheduleGc` schedules a `setTimeout` of `gcTime` through `timeoutManager` for every `Query` and `Mutation` that loses its last observer, which RNTL's `cleanup` makes happen at the end of every spec; `gcTime` defaults to 300 000 ms rather than `Infinity` because jest-expo's setup defines `window`, so `isServer` is false; the timers are created inside React's unmount commit from a promise continuation, never cleared, never `unref`'d. Why nobody saw them: Jest hands spec files to workers, and jest-worker's child never calls `process.exit` on the end message (`processChild.js` only drops its message listener) while the parent SIGTERMs it 500 ms later and SIGKILLs it 500 ms after that, so every handle a spec leaves in a worker dies with the worker and the suite exits at once wherever `maxWorkers` is 2 or more. Jest's `maxWorkers` is `cpus − 1`, and a GitHub-hosted Linux runner for a private repository has two cores (`nproc` 2, `os.cpus().length` 2, measured on this branch), so `maxWorkers` is 1, Jest runs the suite in band in its own process, and the 300-second timers hold Node until they fire. Why MOB-054's `--detectOpenHandles` named nothing on macOS: that flag also forces in-band, which is why the run «lasted five minutes» (the timers), and Jest's collector (`collectHandles.js`) only reports a handle whose creation stack has a test-file or circus frame (`stackIsFromUser`) or whose trigger is a tracked handle; a timer scheduled from a promise continuation has neither (PROMISE resources are skipped), so the gc timers are invisible to it. **Reproduced** before any change. Locally, `jest --ci --runInBand` in client-mobile: 35 suites / 142 tests in 13.4 s, «Jest did not exit one second after the test run has completed», exit 0 at 5 min 00 s after the summary; a scratch `async_hooks` setup file listing every `Timeout` still referenced after each spec file named, after the last of two Client specs, 8 timers of 300 000 ms created by `Query.scheduleGc` ← `Query.removeObserver` ← `QueryObserver.destroy`, 164 such timers across the Staff suite and 326 across mobile-core (`Query.scheduleGc` and `Mutation.scheduleGc`: 24 and 82 mutation timers), plus transient ones (the persister's 1 000 ms, Animated's 16 ms, Jest's reporter 100 ms, and the 5 000 ms hook timeout of the running `afterAll`). On Linux, through a temporary workflow job on this branch (`a4a0b159`, CI run [37824483192](https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/actions/runs/37824483192), job mobile-handle-diagnostic): `nproc` 2, `os.cpus().length` 2, `availableParallelism` 2; `jest --ci --detectOpenHandles src/render-errors.spec.tsx` passed its 2 tests in 39 s and exited 0 at 18:34:34 UTC after starting at 18:28:55 (5 min 39 s) with no «Jest has detected the following open handles» line; the same tracer with `--forceExit` over two specs listed seven 300 000 ms `Query.scheduleGc` timers alive after the last spec. **Built 2026-10-08.** Red `09e41c28`: the three mobile steps of the workflow run `jest --ci` without `--forceExit` (observed failing: the in-band run above, CI run 37819179289 of pull request 17, and the diagnostic job). Green `dc0f3a25`: each of the three `jest.setup.ts` files gives TanStack's `timeoutManager` a provider whose `setTimeout` and `setInterval` return `unref`'d Node timers, so no TanStack timer holds the process; they still fire while a spec runs because Jest's own hook timeout holds it then, so `staleTime`, `gcTime`, retries, and the persister's throttle behave as before; with it the three suites in band exit within a second of their summary (client 14.1 s of tests, staff 25.6 s, mobile-core 8.0 s). Refactor `26fd4445` removes the temporary job and tracer; `3ae461c9` rewrites Test 8 (the mobile paragraph and the CI paragraph: the mechanism, how to see it with `--runInBand`, why `--detectOpenHandles` is blind to it, and that the admin-web step keeps its flag). No app code, API, contract, migration, dependency, or `design/` change; no `eslint-disable`; the largest touched hand-written file is the Client setup at 96 lines. **Verified from a clean shell** (`env -u DATABASE_URL -u NODE_OPTIONS -u TEST_DATABASE_URL`, Node 24.13.0, load average 3–9 during the runs, down from 20 earlier in the session): `pnpm --filter @pilates/tooling lint` exit 0 printing nothing; `eslint .` exit 0 with 0 errors and 0 warnings in mobile-core, client-mobile, and staff-mobile; `format:check` and `tsc --noEmit` clean in all three; Jest `--ci` without `--forceExit`, default workers, captured to files and run twice each: mobile-core 53 suites / 233 tests (4.5 s, 4.2 s), client-mobile 35 / 142 (7.7 s, 7.4 s), staff-mobile 34 / 118 (11.9 s, 12.1 s), every run exit 0 within a second of its summary, 0 `console.error` lines, no «did not exit» and no «Force exiting» line. No simulator run: the change is to three Jest setup files, the workflow, and Test 8; no screen or endpoint moves, so the surface was not exercised and nothing here implies it was. Pull request https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/pull/18, opened as a draft before the fix so the diagnostic job could run, marked ready at the end, for the user to merge (merge commit, never squash). **CI** [37825991628](https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/actions/runs/37825991628) green with the full chain, because the workflow changed: changes 5 s, quality-mobile 1 m 19 s, quality-web 1 m 28 s, quality-api 1 m 46 s, contracts 1 m 16 s, mobile 2 m 08 s without the flag (client-mobile 28 s, staff-mobile 38 s, mobile-core 18 s), web 1 m 59 s, api 6 m 44 s. **Decisions taken under the blanket approval**: (1) the fix is a `timeoutManager` provider with `unref`'d timers in each setup rather than an `afterAll` that clears the query client, because `MutationCache.clear()` only empties its map and never destroys a mutation, so the mutation gc timers would survive a clear; rather than `environmentManager.setIsServer(() => true)`, which would also disable stale timers, refetch intervals, and the focus and online subscriptions (a wider behaviour change); and rather than `gcTime: Infinity` on the client, which is app code and out of scope; (2) the same lines are repeated in the three setups, as the `notifyManager` scheduler already is in the two app setups, because the only home both apps and mobile-core could import from would be a new workspace package (a new dependency), and mobile-core's own setup cannot import the apps; (3) the Linux reproduction was a temporary workflow job on the branch, kept in the history (`a4a0b159`, removed by `26fd4445`), rather than a local Docker container, because the runner is the environment in question and its core count was the open fact; (4) the red commit got no CI run of its own (it would cancel at the 15-minute timeout as run 37819179289 did); its failure is the in-band run, that run, and the diagnostic job; (5) the admin-web step keeps `--forceExit` untouched; (6) the comment on the mobile steps now states the cause (two cores, in band) and points at the setups. **Done 2026-10-08** (thirty-first session). The row is right that interrupted runs leave `pilates_test_<hex>` databases behind and that they are dropped whole. How the context works today: `startDatabaseTestContext` (`test/database/database-test-context.ts`) is called from `beforeAll` by 50 integration specs directly and by `startEvaluationTestWorld` in `evaluation-test-support.ts`, and every caller stops it in `afterAll`. With `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (which must name a `pilates_test_*` admin database) it names a database `pilates_test_` plus 12 hex characters from `randomBytes(6)`, runs `create database` through a one-connection admin pool, migrates it with a synchronous `pnpm exec prisma migrate deploy` (`execFileSync`), and opens a pool; `stop` ends the pool and runs `drop database if exists "<name>" with (force)`. Without it, it starts a `postgres:17-alpine` Testcontainer with a `pilates_test_container` database and `stop` stops the container; nothing is dropped because the database lives inside the container, and Testcontainers' Ryuk reaper removes a container whose test process died (not exercised here: Docker is not running). What the row misses: (1) the only drop is in `stop`, so every path that skips `stop` leaks the database: Ctrl-C (the terminal sends SIGINT to the whole foreground process group, pnpm, Jest, and any running `prisma migrate deploy`), SIGTERM, SIGKILL, or an out-of-memory crash all end the Jest process on the default action without `afterAll`; (2) a failure inside the context after `create database` (a failed migration, or `pnpm` refusing the shell's Node 18) throws out of `beforeAll` before the caller holds a context, so `afterAll`'s `context?.stop()` has nothing to stop; three of the four orphans have no `_prisma_migrations` table at all, which fits a failure before Prisma ran better than a mid-suite interruption; `startEvaluationTestWorld` has the same gap when its fixtures fail after the context started; (3) a Jest timeout: `applyMigrations` blocks the event loop, so the 120 s `testTimeout` cannot fire during a migration, but a `beforeAll` that times out while `create database` is awaited makes Jest run `afterAll` with no context, and the database the late start creates is never dropped; an uncaught error inside a test only fails that test and `afterAll` still runs `stop`, so that case is already covered; (4) a signal handler cannot be registered from the context: `test:integration` runs in band (`--runInBand`, ESM through `--experimental-vm-modules`), so the tests run in the Jest process itself, but each test file sees a sandboxed copy of `process` (`jest-util`'s `createProcessObject` deep-copies it and reruns the EventEmitter constructor on the copy); a throwaway probe spec showed that neither `process.on('SIGTERM')` nor a listener on `import process from 'node:process'` runs when the Jest pid gets SIGTERM, and Jest died on the default action; `@jest/core` 29.7 registers no signal handler of its own, and a Jest `globalTeardown` does not run on a signal either; (5) CI cannot leave databases behind beyond a run: the `api` job's `postgres:17-alpine` service container, with its `pilates_test_ci` admin database and every `pilates_test_<hex>` the suite creates there, is discarded with the runner, so only a local server accumulates them. **Local server on 2026-10-07** (`psql -l`, creation times from each database's `PG_VERSION` file): the four orphans the row names, none with an active connection: `pilates_test_3da52e3326cb` (2026-09-22 11:16), `pilates_test_7384a2a4d627` (2026-09-22 14:11), and `pilates_test_73da0421e248` (2026-09-22 14:17), each empty (no `_prisma_migrations`, about 8.7 MB), and `pilates_test_0d8fe0d94fb4` (2026-09-23 11:06, 12 of today's 22 migrations, 33 application tables, 13 MB); two other `pilates_test_` databases the context did not create, since their names are not the generated 12-hex shape and nothing in the repository names them: `pilates_test_tz` (2026-09-22 01:37, 7 migrations) and `pilates_test_shadow` (2026-09-22 10:22, 8 migrations), listed here and not dropped without the user's say; No simulator or browser surface applies (nothing user-facing changes; the change is test infrastructure only). Pull request https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/pull/8; CI run https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/actions/runs/37697516658 green with the api chain only: changes 5 s, quality-api 1 m 48 s, contracts 1 m 3 s, api 6 m 52 s (unit 116/574, e2e 33/203, integration 66/293, `interrupted-run.integration-spec.ts` 20.5 s, so it ran against the service container rather than returning early); quality-web, web, quality-mobile, and mobile skipped by the paths filter. Decisions taken under the blanket approval: (1) the cleanup is a detached watchdog process per disposable database instead of a signal handler, because a handler registered from the context never runs (Jest's sandboxed `process`, proved by the probe) and a handler in a custom Jest environment would still miss SIGKILL, an out-of-memory crash, and a run that ends without `stop`; the watchdog covers every way the test process can end; (2) it is registered by spawning it with `detached: true` (its own process group, so Ctrl-C reaches Jest but not the watchdog) and `unref()` before `create database`, so no moment exists where the database lives unwatched, and it is removed by `stop`, which drops the database first and then writes `release` and closes its stdin; if the drop in `stop` throws, the watchdog stays armed and drops the database when the process ends; (3) it covers SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGKILL, crashes, a failed migration or failed fixtures after the context started, and a context left running after a Jest timeout, all at the moment the test process ends; a failed start in a still-running suite therefore keeps its empty database until the run ends rather than dropping it on the spot, which was not added because it would be a second mechanism for the same leak; (4) it lives in the context, not a Jest `globalTeardown`, because a global teardown does not run on a signal and does not know the generated names; (5) its scope is one exact name handed over by the process that generated it, refused unless it matches `pilates_test_` plus 12 hex characters, so it can never drop `pilates_test_fixtures`, the admin database, `pilates_test_shadow`, `pilates_test_tz`, or a development database, and nothing anywhere drops by pattern; (6) the watchdog is a `.ts` file run by Node 24's type stripping (no build step, still linted and typechecked; `.nvmrc` pins 24 for CI) and gets the parent's environment with `NODE_OPTIONS` cleared; (7) the Testcontainers path is unchanged: its database lives in a container that Testcontainers' Ryuk removes when the test process dies (not exercised; Docker not running); (8) the red test runs a real child Jest process over a fixture file that only the spec's `--testRegex` selects, so the normal integration and unit regexes never pick it up, and it skips without `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, like the existing context spec; (9) the orphans were confirmed through `pg_database` and `pg_stat_activity` immediately before dropping and dropped with a plain `drop database`, without `with (force)`, so a connection appearing in between would have made the drop fail rather than cut it off. Leftovers: none. `pilates_test_shadow` and `pilates_test_tz` (not generated names; last migrated 2026-09-22 to 7 and 8 of 22 migrations, holding 13 and 145 test rows, named nowhere in the repository or `apps/backend/.env`) were dropped on the user's say on 2026-10-07, after confirming each existed with no active connection, one plain `drop database "<name>"` each, by exact name; the local server now holds only `pilates_test_fixtures` among `pilates_test_` databases. |

| UPL-003 | P1       | Backend/mobile       | Make the transfer-receipt upload fast on a phone network (reported by the user on the Play Internal testing build against production, 2026-10-15: «Subir comprobante» took a long time). Measure first: time each phase in the app (pick, convert, read, declare, PUT, finalize, wait for READY) and on the server (API PUT to R2, worker verification and variants, queue pickup), against production from Bolivia. Likely causes read in the code: (1) `apps/client-mobile/src/uploads/image-upload.ts` sends JPEG and PNG at full resolution (only HEIC and other types are downscaled to 1600 px), so a phone photo or screenshot travels as several megabytes; (2) the file is read into JavaScript as base64 and decoded before the PUT; (3) the bytes go Bolivia → the API in Northflank US Central (0.2 vCPU) → R2 instead of straight to R2; (4) the app then polls every 700 ms (up to 40 times) while the worker, on 0.2 vCPU with pg-boss's default 2 s polling, verifies the image and builds its variants before READY. Candidate fixes, chosen from the measurements: always downscale and re-encode to ADR-0073's largest receipt size before upload, stream the file instead of base64, a pre-signed direct PUT to R2 (an ADR change), marking READY after verification and building variants afterwards, and a shorter worker poll for the upload queue; the Client sees progress meanwhile (MOB-060's busy state) Verify on both platforms and in every app the change reaches (the Client app's receipt and profile photo uploads, and the Staff app if it shares the upload code): the iPhone 16 Pro and iPad Pro 11 Simulators and the Android emulator, recording the device, the steps, and what was seen for each in Evidence (asked by the user on 2026-10-15 after MOB-058). | EXT-002, MOB-060 | done | Recorded 2026-10-15 (fifty-fourth session) at the user's request; any change to where bytes go or when READY is set needs the user's approval first (ADR-0073 and the upload ADRs). **Done 2026-10-16** ([pull request 87](https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/pull/87), branch `fix/upl-003-faster-image-uploads`). **Measured first.** In the app, with temporary never-committed timing logs in `image-upload.ts` on the development builds against a local API and worker (`pilates_dev_sim`), picking a 4288 × 2848 JPEG of 3.05 MB: the iPhone 16 Pro's picker handed over 3.05 MB and the Android emulator's 2.26 MB (its `quality: 0.9` re-encode), unchanged in size, so the PUT carried 2.3–3 MB; the base64 read and decode took 1.1 s on each (on the Mac's CPU, so slower on a phone); hashing 2–3 ms; declare, PUT, and finalize 15–190 ms each on the loopback; READY 1.5 s (iPhone) and 2.3 s (Android) after finalize. On the server, `processing_started_at − created_at` was 30–250 ms and `finalized_at − processing_started_at` (queue pickup plus verification, two variants, stores) 1.26 s and 1.95 s. The worker's verification and receipt variants on one libvips thread (`sharp.concurrency(1)`) cost 310–410 ms of CPU for 3–4 MP photos and 210 ms for a 3.7 MB PNG screenshot, about 1.5–2 s at production's 0.2 vCPU (×5), and 220–230 ms (≈1.1 s) for the same images at 2048 px; queue pickup averages 1 s with pg-boss's default 2 s poll. The PUT itself: from this Mac the production API answers in 170 ms of round trip (`curl` on `/health/ready`), and a phone uplink of 1/3/5 Mbps puts 2.5 MB at 21/7/4 s against 250 KB at 2/0.7/0.4 s. **Production was not timed:** the Mac has no production credentials and an account cannot be created there for the test; Test 53 has the read-only `system.image_assets` query that gives the real PUT and worker times for a phone once the user runs it in the database console. **Dominant cost: the bytes** (2–4 MB over a phone uplink, plus 1 s or more of base64 on the phone), then the worker on 0.2 vCPU (1.5–2 s, about halved by smaller input) and the 2 s queue poll. **Fix** (ordinary optimisations, no change to where bytes go or when READY is set): every picked image is re-encoded once as JPEG at most 2048 px on its longest side, quality 0.8, and the picker hands over the original (`quality: 1`) so nothing is encoded twice (red `8d27a06e` → green `d835ab19`, specs `3300dcbd`); the worker polls `uploads.finalize.v1` every 0.5 s (red `718a5f73` → green `74a35f47`). **After** (same photo, same set-up): 273 KB on Android (8.3× less) and 486 KB on the iPhone (6.3×), a 3.78 MB PNG screenshot 157 KB on the iPad; the re-encode costs 0.1–0.65 s and the read 0.1–0.5 s; READY 0.73–0.81 s after finalize (from 1.5–2.3 s), worker plus pickup 0.75 s (from 1.26–1.95 s). Estimated on a 3 Mbps phone uplink against production: about 11 s before (7 s PUT, 1 s base64, 1 s pickup, 2 s worker) and 3 s after. Options not taken, each needing the user's approval and not worth it now: a pre-signed PUT straight to R2 (ADR-0088; it would save only the API hop of a 250 KB body), READY before the variants (ADR-0073; about 0.5 s left to save), and streaming the file instead of base64 (negligible at 250 KB). **Checks:** client-mobile Jest 41 suites / 179 tests, backend unit 155 / 811, lint, Prettier, and typecheck clean. **Surfaces** (development builds on Metro 8083, API and worker on `pilates_dev_sim`): Android emulator (Medium Phone, API 36, the local debug build of 2026-10-16): Sofía's receipt through a scratch Maestro flow, «Comprobante listo» and «Enviar comprobante» shown, asset 273 554 bytes at 2048 × 1360; Lucía's profile photo by hand with `adb`, the photo in the circle and «Quitar foto». iPhone 16 Pro: the receipt by the scratch flow (486 425 bytes, attached, screenshot checked) and the committed `profile-photo.yaml` passed. iPad Pro 11: the receipt with the PNG screenshot (157 KB, 942 × 2048, the readable variant's text sharp). Until then the rule holds by convention only (the commit skill refuses `main`, the user merges). Readiness line 5 stays unticked (hosting waits for EXT-003). Decisions taken under the blanket approval: (1) the shared setup is a local composite action rather than steps copied into each job, so one file defines the toolchain and the workflow stays one file; (2) action versions pinned to major tags `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `pnpm/action-setup@v6`, `dorny/paths-filter@v3` (the latest majors on 2026-10-07; `sha_pinning_required` is off on the repository); (3) the pnpm store cache is `actions/setup-node`'s `cache: pnpm` (keyed on `pnpm-lock.yaml`) rather than a hand-written `actions/cache` step, one less action and the same key; (4) `.nvmrc` says `24`, not `24.13.0`, so patch releases follow without a commit; (5) a workflow-wide placeholder `DATABASE_URL` on port 1 (`postgresql://nobody@127.0.0.1:1/pilates_ci_unreachable`, the BE-014 convention) satisfies `prisma generate` and the generator without any secret, and the integration suite overrides it per disposable database; (6) the heap flag reaches Jest through the package scripts keeping `${NODE_OPTIONS:-}` instead of the workflow calling Jest directly, so the scripts stay the only definition of how the suites run; 4096 MB because the run needed about 2.8 GB; (7) `--forceExit` on the four frontend suites instead of finding the open handles here (a leftover below), because the suites pass and the handle is not CI's concern; (8) the runner image is pinned to `ubuntu-24.04` because of the announced `ubuntu-latest` migration; (9) timeouts 15 minutes per job and 20 for api, so a hung step fails instead of running to the 6-hour default; (10) concurrency cancels superseded runs on every ref including `main`; (11) the `changes` job uses `dorny/paths-filter` (a third-party action, the standard one) rather than a `git diff` step, because it reads the pull request's file list through the API and needs no deep checkout; (12) `packages/api-contracts/**` triggers all three chains because `check:api` forces every contract change to touch the committed generated client, so a backend change that alters the contract always runs web and mobile too; (13) pushes to `main` ignore the filter so `main` always has a full green record; (14) the referral spec fix (a `waitFor` around the first balance read) was made here rather than queued, because a flaky required check would block every pull request; (15) the three-job split the user asked for mid-item was reverted with a revert commit, not a force push, so the branch history stayed linear; (16) the scratch proofs used force pushes and resets on their own throwaway branches, never on an item branch; (17) the row's description was rewritten to the user's redefinition instead of keeping the four-job text, because the user changed the definition, not the count. Leftovers, not taken: the open handles that keep the admin-web and mobile Jest processes alive on Linux (`--detectOpenHandles` from a Linux shell; likely the five-minute TanStack Query garbage-collection timer and MSW); the integration suite's in-band memory growth (~30 MB per suite file, 65 files), which the heap flag covers but does not cure; `apps/backend/package.json`'s `lint` glob still names non-existent `apps` and `libs` directories (BE-015 leftover); MOB-050 (mobile lint) still needs a row; the act() warnings the client-mobile and staff-mobile suites print on every run (24 000 log lines on the runner) are noise, not failures. **Closed by decision 2026-10-08** (thirty-first session, branch `chore/ext-004-record-no-main-protection`). The CI half was done on 2026-10-07 and is unchanged. The coding standards sentence that claimed `main` is protected is corrected in the same pull request. ### Cost of each gate (researched 2026-10-12)

Prices from the providers' pages or, where marked ~, from third-party trackers;
confirm on the provider's page before paying. Billing: **once**, **year**,
**month**, or **usage**.

| Service | What we use it for | Plan we use | Price | Billing | Next step up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub Actions | CI, preview cleanup (EXT-007), preview-origin registration (WEB-019), deploy jobs | Free | $0 within 2,000 private-repo minutes | usage: ~$0.006 per Linux minute beyond | — |
| Render | Shared development API for previews | Free (sleeps when idle) | $0 | — | — |
| Neon | Shared development database | Free | $0 | — | — |
| Vercel | Admin web previews and production, `/api/v1` proxy, ADR-0087 middleware | Hobby, also for production by decision | $0 within 100 GB transfer and 1M middleware invocations a month | — | — |
| Expo / EAS | Build, sign, and submit both apps; over-the-air updates | Free | $0: 15 iOS and 15 Android builds, 60 workflow minutes, updates to 1,000 monthly users | month | Starter $19 a month ($45 build credit), then ~$1–4 a build |
| Firebase Cloud Messaging | Android push delivery behind Expo Push | Free | $0 | — | — |
| Better Stack | Uptime checks, worker heartbeat, error alerts | Free (account open since 2026-10-13) | $0: 10 monitors and 10 heartbeats, 3-minute checks at the fastest, 100k exceptions a month, 3 GB logs for 3 days, email and Slack alerts only | — | $29 a seat a month (annual) or $34 (monthly) |
| Resend (since 2026-10-19, ADR-0094) | Verification, activation, recovery, and email-change messages | Free | $0: 3,000 emails a month, 100 a day, 1 domain; a launch-day burst over 100 fails after its retries | month | Pro $20 a month: 50,000 emails, no daily limit |
| Cloudflare R2 | Receipt, profile-photo, and Promotion images | Free allowance (since 2026-10-14; card on file) | $0 within 10 GB-month, 1M writes, 10M reads; egress free | usage: $0.015 per GB-month, $4.50 per million writes, $0.36 per million reads | — |
| Northflank | Production API and worker | Developer Sandbox (since 2026-10-13; card on file for verification only) | $0: 2 always-on services, 2 jobs, 1 addon, up to $20 a month of resources; nf-compute-20 (0.2 vCPU, 512 MB, ~$5.40 a month of the allowance) is the largest plan allowed; free projects only in US Central or Europe West | — | usage: $0.01667 per vCPU-hour (~$12 a month), $0.00833 per GB-hour of memory (~$6 a month); smallest plan $2.70 a month |
| Aiven PostgreSQL | Production database with backups | Free (since 2026-10-13) | $0: 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM, 1 GB disk, 20 connections, no pooler, one disaster-recovery backup without point-in-time restore, no SLA, PostgreSQL 18 only, cloud picked by Aiven, powered off after a notice when idle | — | ~Hobbyist $12 a month (8 GB), ~Startup $60–75 a month |
| Domain (`.com` at Cloudflare) | Email sender records, API and admin hostnames, privacy-policy and support pages, mobile links | — | ~$10.46 | year | `.bo` ~€130–300 a year through resellers |

| Apple Developer Program | iOS device builds, TestFlight, App Store, APNs push, Universal Links | — | $99 | year | — |
| D-U-N-S number | Only if the stores' accounts are the studio's (organization) | — | $0 | — | up to 30 days to arrive |

### Order to open the gates (revised 2026-10-12: cheapest and fastest first; gate 6 opened 2026-10-14)

Every code item without an account gate is done, so this order is the
project's priority order. On 2026-10-12 the user asked to spend as little as
possible while the studio is not operating, so gates are opened by price and
lead time, and paid store accounts wait until shortly before launch. (The
2026-10-07 order put the domain, SendPulse, and Apple before hosting.)

1. GitHub with Actions → EXT-004: done; `main` is protected by convention only
   (decision 2026-10-08).
2. Render + Neon and Vercel previews → EXT-003's development half, WEB-010's
   preview part, WEB-019, WEB-020: done. Retired 2026-10-17 by EXT-016 (ADR-0091).
3. Better Stack (free) → EXT-003's monitors: done 2026-10-13; the readiness
   monitor moved to the production API at gate 4, and the worker heartbeat
   has run since the production worker started (2026-10-14).
4. Northflank Developer Sandbox + Aiven free → EXT-003's production half on
   the providers' own hostnames, then WEB-010's production deploy on Vercel
   Hobby: done 2026-10-13, without a worker (gates 5 and 7), a deploy
   workflow (EXT-008), or the daily dump (EXT-009).
5. Cloudflare R2 (free allowance, card on file) → EXT-002: done 2026-10-14,
   with the production worker; EXT-009's daily dump and first restore drill:
   done 2026-10-14, so production may hold real Client data.
6. Expo/EAS (free) → REL-001's account half: EAS projects for both apps and
   development builds, then NOT-002 (push delivery, verified with a free
   Firebase project on the Android emulator and with `xcrun simctl push` on
   the iOS Simulators). Opened 2026-10-14 by the user's decision, which
   reverses the 2026-10-12 hold («until shortly before the store accounts»);
   builds stay few, and each step states how many of the free plan's monthly
   builds it spends before it starts. Real iOS push still waits for gate 9
   (APNs key).
7. Domain (~$10.46 a year), as late as possible by the user's decision
   (2026-10-12); gate 8 no longer waits for it (2026-10-15). Opened
   2026-10-15: `emmapilatesstudio.com` with Email Routing (EXT-014 done). Resend (free, ADR-0094, replacing
   SendPulse) sends from our own address with it (EXT-001), and the closed test's testers cannot
   register without verification and activation emails. It also gives LNK-001
   its link domain and the stores their privacy-policy and support pages.
8. Google Play ($25 once), about three weeks before launch → the Android
   halves of REL-001, NOT-002, and LNK-001, starting the 14-day closed test.
   Started 2026-10-15. By the user's decision the same day, gate 8 no longer
   waits for gate 7: the goal is to test the apps through the Play Store,
   so REL-002 (the Play account) starts now, followed by REL-003 to REL-006
   up to Internal testing. The privacy policy is hosted without our own
   domain until WEB-021, the support email is the owner's address, and a
   Client tester's verification link is read from the production worker
   until EXT-001 sends email. The closed test's outside testers and REL-007
   still need EXT-014, EXT-001, and WEB-021.
9. Apple Developer ($99 a year), one to two weeks before launch → REL-001's
   iOS release, NOT-002's iOS push, LNK-001's Universal Links, and REL-010's
   real-email link test on both platforms.
10. Studio business data and production secrets → the production
    configuration at go-live.

FUT-001 stays deferred.

**Handoff addendum (2026-10-15, fifty-second session: NOT-002 cold-start push taps).** One Android `preview` build (11 of 30 this month) confirmed that a push tapped while the app's process is dead does not route on a build without the development client either. The cause is Expo's activity wrapper, which drops the tap's `onNewIntent` while expo-updates delays the app's load; the new config plugin `@pilates/mobile-core/launch-tap-plugin` forwards the tap to expo-notifications (NOT-002's row, «Cold-start follow-up»). The fix was verified on a local Gradle release build, not on a second EAS build; both apps need a new native build before devices get it. [pull request 61](https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/pull/61) (branch `fix/not-002-cold-start-push-tap`) waits for the user's merge. The `preview` EAS channel and branch were created by that build. `pilates_dev_sim` holds more cancelled Sessions and notifications for Lucía; rebuild it before the next Maestro run (Test 19). **Next to pull:** the user's pick.

## Production readiness checklist

Nothing reaches real users until each line is done:

- [x] Sessions materialize without fixtures (BKM-003) and empty Sessions cancel themselves (BOOK-004).
- [x] First Administrator bootstrap command and runbook (IDN-006); a production run still needs real email (EXT-001).
- [ ] Real email templates and Resend delivery (EML-001, EXT-001); R2 storage (EXT-002; the variants exist since UPL-002).
- [ ] Push delivery and store builds (NOT-002, REL-001) with Universal/App Links (LNK-001).
- [ ] Hosting, CI, secrets, staged migrations, and monitoring (EXT-003, BE-005 gaps, BE-003).
- [ ] Data governance: Account closure, personal-data and Evaluation retention, audit retention, backups, restore drills, incident runbooks (BE-006, BE-007, BE-008).
- [ ] Staff management and admin web for studio operation (IDN-007, ADM-001, BKO-001/002, WEB-001–WEB-010).
- [ ] Real transfer instructions and production secrets configured (see the gate table above).
- [x] Staging mirrors production and the staging app builds install beside the store apps (EXT-017).
- [x] The backend suites are green with no operator-set environment (BE-014): the e2e suite boots without a database and the unit suite needs no `--experimental-vm-modules`.

Reuse decisions: admin web writes its own `formatBolivianos` and Bolivia-time helpers because `@pilates/mobile-core` is a React Native package and its formatter drops the decimals ADR-0082 and the design system show; a shared `CatalogPage` layout was extracted when the second catalog page appeared and Sucursales moved onto it; `ChoiceChips` is shared by the frequency and scope choices; the API-002 query was extended rather than duplicated. Gaps: native date and time pickers follow the browser's language (an English Chrome shows `09/29/2026` and `09:00 AM`), so dd/mm/aaaa and 24-hour pickers need custom controls or a Spanish browser; cancelled Sessions are not drawn (AW02 shows a «Cancelada» legend); the bundle is 675 kB, so route-level splitting is due before WEB-010; the `booking-command` reschedule spec needs a fixed clock (its own item); dev fixtures reapplied do not remove Sessions or schedules created by hand. Decisions taken under the blanket approval: AW28 lists transfers only, because cash and Credit-only Payments are confirmed when recorded, cannot be rejected, and never wait for review (booking CONTEXT, Payment; ADR-0006; AW28 «every transfer Payment»; AW29 «solo llegan transferencias»); a new paged admin-web operation instead of widening the Staff app's pending-only array (ADR-0061/0062, ADR-0016); the backend's `status` defaults to `all` while the screen opens on Pendiente (AW28), and in Todos pending rows come first, oldest first, then decided ones newest decision first; `pendingCount` rides on every page so the subtitle and the sidebar badge need no second endpoint; the list refuses non-Administrators with `administration_access_denied` like the other admin-web oversight reads, while the Staff app's review endpoints keep `booking_access_denied` (the admin web only branches on 403); the receipt is shown from the existing authenticated, `no-store` `…/receipt` route through the same-origin proxy and the host-only session cookie rather than a new five-minute signed URL: ADR-0071's concern is a bearer URL that leaks, and this route is not a credential by itself (an ended session or a deleted receipt shows «No pudimos mostrar el comprobante.» and Reintentar re-reads the review, which the session guard turns into Login); the image never enters the query cache; «Confirmar pago» asks first because it starts the Subscription and cannot be undone, while «Rechazar» keeps AW29's inline reason with «Confirmar rechazo» as its explicit second step (follow-up 55 §4); a conflict re-reads the review and tells a Payment decided elsewhere from one refused because the Client already holds an active Plan by the review's state, since both answer `payment_confirmation_conflict`; confirming never extends an active Subscription (the backend refuses it, unchanged); a decision refreshes every Payment list and that review, plus the Clientes directory and every Client detail after a confirmation (her Plan starts, and a first Payment may award Credit to a referrer the admin web cannot name) or only her detail after a rejection (reserved Credit released), and a conflict refreshes like a confirmation (asserted in `payment-decision-cache.spec.ts`); the review has `staleTime: 0` so each opening is current; the open panel stays in local state like WEB-003/004. Reuse decisions: `CatalogPage` gained `canOpen` and `panelDescription` (and `DataTable` `canClickRow`) instead of a payments-only list layout; `ConfirmDialog` gained a primary tone; AW22's summary rows were extracted for AW29; `SearchFilter`, `ListFilter`, `StatusPill`, `PageNotice`, `QueryFailure`/`LoadingNotice`, `SidePanel`, `formatBolivianos`, `boliviaParts`/`formatCivilDate`, `initials`, and the form primitives are reused; the receipt viewer follows the Staff app's behavior (thumbnail, «Ampliar»/«Ver en grande», full screen, no actions in the viewer) but not its code, because the Staff app fetches bytes into a data URI for React Native while the browser can load the authenticated route directly. Open questions for the user (money and data governance, not decided): what a rejection reason may contain, given the Client reads it verbatim in her app and notification (for example no bank details or other Clients' data) and whether it needs a list of standard reasons; whether reading a receipt or the Payment list should be audited (ordinary reads are not, ADR-0055); whether a decided receipt should stay viewable in the admin web for its 7-day post-decision window (today only pending rows open, as AW28 draws); how long rejected Payments and their reasons are kept (BE-007). Gaps: the sidebar count refreshes on this browser's decisions and page loads, not live when the Staff app decides (no background polling exists); the receipt route has no signed-URL variant for a future CDN; narrow rows use the shared labelled-card reflow rather than AW28's compact «Plan · fecha» card; the bundle grew to 715 kB, so route-level splitting is due before WEB-010; valid activation links still cannot be opened from the local email capture. Decisions taken under the blanket approval: AW17 is an unpaged card list, not a `CatalogPage` table, with no search and no Branch scope; the state pill tones are Borrador neutral, Programada Advertencia, Activa Éxito, Finalizada Error (like «Venció» in Mi plan); the order on screen is the saved one until a drop, a drop persists the whole list and the answer replaces the cache (no optimistic renumbering, so no equal positions ever show), a refused drop restores the saved order with a role=alert line; keyboard reordering is the accessible route the handle must offer; the thumbnail and the 1440 px preview are plain `<img>` elements on the private route with the session cookie, never in the query cache, with the asset id appended to the URL; «Publicar» disabled until every field exists (follow-up 39) while «Guardar borrador» always saves; a published Promotion's footer is «Guardar cambios» / «Dejar de publicar» and only an image change turns it into the draft pair; «Publicar» on a new Promotion creates then publishes, and if the publish step fails the panel keeps the created row so a retry publishes instead of creating twice; delete asks first and archives (BKM-001); the image is checked in the browser (format, weight, decoded size) before the three calls, and a refused file never leaves the browser; the worker's `failed` verdict shows a generic message because the status route names no reason; the same `Idempotency-Key` per typed body for create, a fresh UUID per finalize; the window line and the image-change warning use the typed dates and the saved row, not a re-read; no drag library: pointer events and the existing primitives suffice (about 200 lines, no dependency commit). Reuse decisions: the browser upload stays in the admin web (`api/upload-image.ts`) rather than a shared package: the Client app's `receipt-upload.ts` reads files, hashes, and picks images through Expo and ends by attaching a receipt, so only the four-call order (about 25 lines) is common, and the next user is the mobile profile photo (Client 22), which would be Expo again; extract a runtime-neutral protocol package at that third user if the order changes; `useIdempotencyKey`/`idempotencyHeaders`, `ConfirmDialog`, `SidePanel`, `PageHeader`, `PageNotice`, `QueryFailure`/`LoadingNotice`, `StatusPill`, `formatCivilDate`/`boliviaToday`/`addDays`, `civilDateField` (added beside `pastCivilDateField`), the form primitives, and `closeButtonClass` are reused; `optionalSearch` was added to `components/table/pagination.ts` for every list route. Backend proposals (not done, no migration): expose the worker's reason on `UploadStatusDto` (`failureReason`) so the admin web can say `image_dimensions_too_small` / `image_animated_not_allowed` instead of the generic line; keep the original filename on the image asset (or accept «Imagen actual» in AW18, follow-up 61 §3); the `promotion_1440` variant of a source narrower than 1440 px loses 16:9 (sharp's `withoutEnlargement` with `cover` made 1200 × 810 from a 1200 × 1600 file, while 480 and 960 were exact): size the box from the source width in `uploads/image-variants.ts`; UPL-002's review DTO `mediaType` gap stands. Open questions for the user (data governance and product, not decided): how long archived Promotions and their audit history are kept (BE-007, UPL-002's question stands); what a Promotion may show beyond the 80/280 characters; whether a Promotion whose window ended should be re-publishable without a new window (the API allows it); whether reordering should be audited (UPL-002 left it unaudited). Gaps: the mid-drag visual (tilt, dimming, insertion line) was verified in Playwright, not screenshotted in the walk; the worker's refusal reason is generic until the status route carries it; the file picker filters formats through `accept`, so only a dropped file reaches the format refusal; Firefox and WebKit journeys still need `playwright install`; the Client carousel (MOB-019) is still not built. **Design follow-up 39 exported 2026-09-30** (`76a6f95`, status `5623d3b`): applied on a temporary Claude Design canvas (no TurboTenant design system), read back and copied byte for byte, rendered over a scratch copy of `design/` and checked against checklist 30 before the copy; the canvas was deleted. Decisions taken under the blanket approval: **Categorías de gasto is studio-wide** (BKO-001 D13: one set of labels for every Branch), so AW15 has no Branch column, the selector shows its studio-wide note there, and follow-up 56 §1 asks the design system and AW34 to say so; the Supply list became page-and-offset with a status filter rather than client-side paging over the array (ADR-0061/0062, as WEB-003 did), and the low-stock count rides on every page so the sidebar needs no second endpoint; the sidebar count and both movement panels read the same one-page-of-100 active list, so a movement refreshes both at once; AW08 shows only active Supplies and AW31's filter every Supply including archived ones; a Withdrawal or Supply rename/archive refreshes that Branch's Supply lists and withdrawal history, a create or Restock only its Supply lists (a Restock adds no Withdrawal), never another Branch's (asserted in `back-office-cache.spec.ts`); a Salary Payment refreshes every payroll page and only the all-Branches expense report (payroll is studio-wide, BKO-001 Q3); an Expense refreshes its Branch's Expenses, that Branch's and the all-Branches report, and the category list (its «En uso»); a category change refreshes only the category list; the stock shown next to each Insumo lives in the option label, which is «next to the selected item» on every browser; the withdrawal quantity is checked against the stock last read and a server refusal re-reads it, the database keeping the last word (D4); the Idempotency-Key is kept per request body, so a retried lost answer replays and an edited body never reuses a key (`idempotency_key_reused`); Withdrawals and Restocks have no edit or delete anywhere (immutable, D6) and Salary Payments and Expenses only a correction (Q1); dates are no later than today in Bolivia on the client and the server (Q2); the Expense's Branch is shown as a line in its panel because AW14 has no field for it (D11); deleting an unused category asks first because it cannot be undone; the AW31 month picker is a stepper instead of a native month input, which Safari and Firefox do not draw; the history link carries `?page=1&pageSize=20` because TanStack Router's types require search for the nested route. Reuse decisions: `CatalogPage` gained panel actions and links instead of a second list layout for AW08; `DataTable`, `SidePanel`, `ConfirmDialog`, `ListFilter`, `StatusPill`, `PageNotice`, `QueryFailure`/`LoadingNotice`, the form primitives, `wholeNumberField`, `formatBolivianos`, `formatCivilDate`/`formatCivilMoment`, and the sidebar badge are reused; Horario's key predicate and no-Branch page were extracted at their second use; the Plan form's bolivianos field was extracted for the two Back Office amounts; one `CategoryAdder` serves AW14 and AW15; one problem mapper serves every Back Office code. Gaps: Restocks have no read-back screen (AW31 lists Withdrawals only); native date pickers follow the browser's language (`mm/dd/yyyy` in an English Chrome), as in WEB-003; the Insumos count refreshes on this browser's changes and page loads, not live; the movement panels and AW31's filter read at most 100 Supplies per Branch; AW31 keeps a `supplyId` from another Branch after the selector changes (it shows the empty state); the bundle grew to 753 kB, so route-level splitting is due before WEB-010; Back Office still has no unit-level specs (its adapters are integration-tested and the new transport parser is covered by e2e); AW16 (WEB-009) still has to combine `reports/income` and `reports/expenses`. Decisions taken under the blanket approval: lazy components sit on the route's `component` (not inside a wrapper) so intent preload fetches the chunk before the click, and the wrapper modules use `getRouteApi` by id rather than importing the route object, which would be a circular import; no `pendingComponent` was added, so the main area is blank for the milliseconds a cold chunk takes (the sidebar hover preload covers the usual case), recorded as a gap; the sign-in pages stay in the entry because they are the first thing a visitor needs; `preloadAdminPages` is exported from `router.tsx` because it is also what a browser would call to warm the pages after Login; a foreign filter is forgotten by an effect once the options are known (and page 1 restored), never by rendering a select whose value has no option; the select keeps its native element (ADR-0040 prefers semantic HTML) and only its arrow changes; Playwright journeys start each from a fresh sign-in and share one database in file order, so the Expense journey runs on the empty Gastos the fixtures leave; the session-expiry journey revokes the session through `page.request` (the browser's own cookie jar) because the 30-minute idle expiry cannot be waited for, and it ends in the same `401 authentication_required` path; the authorization journey is the Assistant's neutral refusal plus the `untrusted_origin` refusal, because the fixtures hold one Administrator, a second one cannot be activated without the email capture, and Paola cannot demote herself, so the page's 403 state stays component-tested (every list spec covers it); Playwright's `webServer` was not used because it starts before `globalSetup` and the database name is only known there; the teardown is the function `globalSetup` returns; the e2e backend runs on 3101 so a development backend on 3100 is never disturbed; only Chromium is configured because it is the one browser cached (the config names the `playwright install` step for the others). MOB-057 found the mobile cause (two cores, in band, TanStack's five-minute gc timers) and left the admin-web step with its flag because that suite «lingers on an open handle on Linux for good». **Compared with the code 2026-10-08** (thirty-second session, branch `chore/web-016-admin-web-jest-handle`, from `main` with pull requests 18 and 19 merged). What each piece of the setup holds open: `jest.environment.cjs` copies seventeen Node globals into jsdom (fetch, Request, Response, Headers, FormData, Blob, File, the text codecs, the three streams, `BroadcastChannel`, `MessageChannel`, `MessagePort`, `structuredClone`) and replaces the abort pair and `crypto`; of these only a `BroadcastChannel` or a `MessagePort` can hold the process, and only once something in the jsdom context constructs one and listens on it. MSW (`msw/node` 2.15.0): `useMockServer` in `src/test/msw.ts` is the only lifecycle, every spec that renders or calls `server.use` calls it (checked file by file), so `server.close()` is reached in every file; its WebSocket support creates one module-level `BroadcastChannel` in `lib/core/ws.js` and `unref`s it at once (`hasRefCounted`), so it holds nothing; its interceptors (ClientRequest, XMLHttpRequest, fetch, WebSocket) patch functions and own no handle. TanStack Query 5.102.2: `createAdminQueryClient` sets `staleTime` 30 s and leaves `gcTime` at its 300 000 ms default (jsdom defines `window`, so `isServer` is false), and the tracer below saw its `Query.scheduleGc` and `Mutation.scheduleGc` timers after every rendering spec, but they are scheduled through jsdom's `window.setTimeout` and jest-environment-jsdom's teardown closes the window, which clears them: a minute after a spec none was left. The router is TanStack Router on a memory history with no timer of its own; `test/` holds only the CSS stub and fixtures; `e2e/support/child-process.test.ts` spawns two Node children and kills both inside its tests (their `PROCESSWRAP` and pipe die with them). The never-ending handle is React's `scheduler` 0.27.0: at module load it takes `setImmediate` if defined (Jest's jsdom environment leaves it out), else a `MessageChannel` if defined, else `setTimeout`; with the environment's copy of Node's `MessageChannel` in scope it builds one and sets `port1.onmessage`, and a Node `MessagePort` with a message listener is a referenced handle that nothing ever closes, one per spec file's module registry. Why MOB-057's five-minute pattern does not fit: a timer ends by itself and jsdom clears these anyway; a listening port never ends, so the process lives until it is killed. **Reproduced** before any change (load average 17–23 throughout the session: another project's Jest workers were running on the Mac). `jest --ci --runInBand` in `apps/admin-web` from a clean shell: 65 suites, 417 tests (one `supply-movements` test timed out at 5 s under the load), summary at 225 s, «Jest did not exit one second after the test run has completed», and the process still alive at 0 % CPU 10 m 46 s after its start (seven minutes after the summary) when it was killed; `plans-page.spec.tsx` alone in band likewise never exited (killed six and a half minutes after its summary). A scratch `async_hooks` setup file passed as a second `--setupFilesAfterEnv` (listing every resource except promises with its creation stack, printing the ones still `hasRef()` after each spec and, through an `unref`'d Node interval, every minute afterwards) named, one and three minutes after the plans spec, exactly one referenced handle: `MESSAGEPORT` created from `scheduler.development.js:221` while `scheduler/index.js` loaded, with the 300 000 ms gc timers gone. On Linux, through a temporary workflow job on this branch (`d6f448f0`, `9970ecd0`; CI run [37833729875](https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/actions/runs/37833729875), job web-handle-diagnostic): `nproc` 2, `os.cpus().length` 2, `availableParallelism` 2; the whole suite under `timeout 780` without `--forceExit` passed 65 / 417 in 253.9 s with its summary at 19:47:12 UTC, printed «did not exit», and was killed by `timeout` (exit 124) at 19:55:57, 8 m 45 s later, with the tracer's last report still listing referenced `MESSAGEPORT`s and nothing else that could hold the process. **Built 2026-10-08.** Red `5171ab46`: the `web` step runs `jest --ci` without `--forceExit` (observed failing: the in-band runs above and the diagnostic job). Green `e339466e`: `jest.environment.cjs` no longer copies `MessageChannel` and `MessagePort` into jsdom (nothing the specs load needs them: a search of msw, `@mswjs/interceptors`, TanStack, Radix, Testing Library, and react-dom found only `react-dom-server.browser`, which no spec loads), so the scheduler falls back to `setTimeout` as in any jsdom environment; with it one rendering spec in band exits at once and the whole suite in band exits within a second of its summary. Pull request https://github.com/DaleneyRuben/emma-pilates/pull/22, opened as a draft at the red so the job could run, marked ready at the end, for the user to merge (merge commit, never squash). **Decisions taken under the blanket approval**: (1) the job runs the root `pnpm test:admin-e2e` script, rebuilding the backend and the admin web in the job (about 35 s on the runner) rather than passing `dist/` from quality-api and quality-web as artifacts, so the scripts stay the only definition of how the suite runs (EXT-004's reading) and the web chain does not wait on the api chain; (2) the admin database is `pilates_test_ci`, made by the same `psql` step as the api job, on the job's own service container (each job has its own runner, nothing is shared); (3) the browser install lives in the shared setup action behind a `playwright-browser` input that defaults to `"false"`, so the other seven jobs pay nothing and the workflow keeps one setup; (4) the cache is `actions/cache@v6` on `~/.cache/ms-playwright` keyed `playwright-chromium-<os>-<version>` with the version read from `playwright --version` (so a bump of the pinned version misses once and saves), `playwright install chromium` only on a miss, `install-deps` on every run because apt packages are not part of the download; the full Chromium rather than `--only-shell` (the headless shell alone would be smaller, but the download is cached and the full build is what the browser walks use); (5) the failure artifact is `actions/upload-artifact@v7` of `apps/admin-web/test-results/` alone (no HTML report: the reporter on CI is `github`), named `web-e2e-test-results`, seven days' retention, `if-no-files-found: ignore`; (6) the teardown gains one `console.log` naming the dropped database, a configuration-level change with no invented test (the global setup spawns servers and is exercised by every run); (7) the service block is copied from the api job rather than shared through a YAML anchor, as the workflow's other blocks are; (8) `BOOT_WITHOUT_JOB_RUNTIME` is not set, because the job runtime boots on the disposable database exactly as it does locally; (9) the job's timeout is 15 minutes like the other frontend jobs; (10) the pull request was opened as a draft at the red so the runner could show the failure (as WEB-016 did) and the red commit's run is kept in the history; ## Updating this backlog

Every edit to this file reaches `main` through a pull request like any other change (coding standards, «Branches and pull requests»). When starting work, change one item to `in progress`. When completing it, change
it to `done` and replace Evidence with the commit hash. If implementation exposes
a missing product rule, mark the item `blocked`, record the exact question in the
row or owning context, and resolve it before continuing that behavior.
